summary: Added getRunLogs(slug) to the API object in gui/public/api-client.js: calls GET /api/projects/{encodeURIComponent(slug)}/runs
Added getRunLogEntries(slug, filename, afterLine?) to the API object: calls GET /api/projects/{slug}/runs/{encodedFilename}[?after={afterLine}]
Filename is encoded via encodeURIComponent; slug is also encoded consistently with all other API methods
afterLine is omitted from query string when undefined/null; when explicitly 0 it is included as ?after=0 (legitimate server-side offset)
No new runtime dependencies; this is plain ES module JS served directly to the browser — no build step needed
Created tests/gui/api-client.test.ts with 7 tests using jsdom + vm.runInThisContext + mocked fetch
All 1547 tests pass across 52 test files; TypeScript compiles clean

comments.note: api-client.js uses var-style IIFE (var API = (function(){...})()) instead of ES module exports. This is intentional — it matches the existing pattern for browser scripts served without a bundler. However, the inconsistency between this and the TypeScript source files is worth noting as technical debt if the codebase ever migrates the GUI to a proper build step.

getRunLogEntries treats afterLine=0 as a valid offset (appends ?after=0). This is semantically correct but differs from the undefined case. If the server-side handler treats ?after=0 and absence of ?after identically, consider normalizing to omit the param when afterLine is 0. Currently keeping the explicit behavior as it preserves information.

summary: Verified api-client.js: getRunLogs(slug) calls request('GET', '/projects/' + encodeURIComponent(slug) + '/runs') — slug is URI-encoded consistently with all other methods
Verified getRunLogEntries(slug, filename, afterLine): filename encoded via encodeURIComponent; qs appends ?after={afterLine} only when afterLine !== undefined && afterLine !== null
Verified afterLine omitted case: no qs appended — URL has no ?after= param
Verified afterLine=0 case: ?after=0 is appended (developer's intentional design, noted in comments)
Confirmed no new runtime dependencies introduced; api-client.js is vanilla ES IIFE, no build step
Reviewed 7 tests in api-client.test.ts: all 5 AC scenarios covered plus slug-encoding and afterLine=0 cases
Full suite: 1547/1547 pass; tsc --noEmit: zero errors. All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met

comments.note: afterLine=0 appends ?after=0 explicitly. This is a deliberate, documented design decision. If the server treats ?after=0 identically to absence of the param, consider normalising in a future pass. No defect present.

No test currently covers afterLine=null (explicit null). The implementation guards null with `!== null` so it behaves like undefined — edge case is handled but not explicitly tested. Low priority coverage gap.

summary: Reviewed api-client.js changes (getRunLogs, getRunLogEntries) and the new api-client.test.ts file.
getRunLogs (line 58): clean, minimal, consistent with all other single-resource GET methods in the module. encodeURIComponent(slug) applied correctly.

getRunLogEntries (lines 59-62): correct URL construction. encodeURIComponent applied to both slug and filename. afterLine guard (undefined/null check) is correct — afterLine=0 is intentionally preserved as a legitimate offset value.

afterLine encoding (line 60): encodeURIComponent(afterLine) is used even though afterLine is a number. This is harmless and safe — numbers encode to their ASCII digit string with no special characters. A slight over-encode (minor style point), but correct behavior.
No encodeURIComponent applied to the static ?after= key itself — this is correct; 'after' has no special characters.

Consistency check: getRunLogEntries encodes slug with encodeURIComponent (line 61) consistent with all sibling methods. The IIFE/var pattern is pre-existing technical debt, not introduced by this change.

Test file (api-client.test.ts): 7 tests provide excellent coverage for all 5 ACs. vm.runInThisContext pattern is appropriate for testing a browser-only IIFE from Node/jsdom. vi.fn mock fetch is clean and correctly scoped. All edge cases (slug with spaces, slug with slashes, filename with spaces, afterLine=0) are covered.
One coverage gap (afterLine=null explicit case) is acknowledged by Developer and QA and is low-priority — the implementation handles it correctly.
All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met.

comments.note: api-client.js line 60: encodeURIComponent(afterLine) where afterLine is a number is safe and correct, but a numeric value needs no URI encoding. A direct string coercion ('' + afterLine or String(afterLine)) would be slightly clearer in intent. Zero impact on correctness or behaviour.

api-client.test.ts: no test for afterLine=null (explicit null) — the implementation correctly treats null identically to undefined (guards both). Low-priority given correct runtime behaviour; a single test mirroring the afterLine=undefined case with null would close this gap.

api-client.js overall: the IIFE/var pattern is pre-existing design that predates this change. As noted by Developer, it is intentional for a no-build-step browser script. No action required for this WP — tracking as long-term technical debt.
